name: Claude API programmatic tool calling + code execution tool
engine: Anthropic-hosted Linux container (Python 3.11, x86_64, 1 CPU, 5 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk); REPL state persists with container reuse
how_run: Not run: no API key on this machine. Documented entry point is a Messages API request with the code_execution_20260120+ tool and allowed_callers: ["code_execution_20260120"] on each client tool.

P1.detail: Docs only, not run. "Tools that allow a code execution caller are exposed to Claude's code as async Python functions ... Each function takes a single dict of arguments and returns a string: the text of the tool_result you send back." Each call pauses the code and surfaces a tool_use block with caller.type code_execution_20260120 to the client.

P2.detail: Docs state the result carries stdout and stderr: "code_execution_result", "stdout": ..., "stderr": ..., "return_code". Docs are silent on stdout truncation for a 200,000-char print and on whether a final bare expression is echoed. The bash sub-tool has an output_file_too_large error: "Command output exceeded the maximum size" (size not given).

P3.detail: Docs: "Internet access: Completely disabled for security" and "External connections: No outbound network requests allowed". Not run. Resolves the survey's open item.

P4.detail: Code runs in Anthropic's container, so the client's /etc/hosts is unreachable by construction. Docs: "Sandbox isolation: Full isolation from host system and other containers" and "File access: Limited to workspace directory only". Reading the container's own /etc/hosts is undocumented.

P5.detail: PROBE_SECRET in the client process is never sent to the container (inference from architecture). Docs are silent on environment variables inside the container.

P6.detail: Docs: "each REPL cell also has a 90-second wall-clock limit"; a cell that exceeds it "returns a normal code execution result with a non-zero return_code and a detection_timeout status message". A whole tool call past the (unstated) maximum returns execution_time_exceeded. A pending host tool call times out after about 4 minutes: "TimeoutError: Calling tool ['query_database'] timed out (no response after 270s)."

P7.detail: Docs: "Memory: The container has 5 GiB of RAM." Behaviour at the limit (OOM text) is not documented.

P8.detail: Persists only when the client passes the container ID back. Docs: "With code_execution_20260120 or later and programmatic tool calling, the Python interpreter state (such as variable bindings) also persists across requests that reuse the container." Without it: "Each request runs in a new container". Containers expire 30 days after creation; checkpointed after about 5 minutes idle.

P9.detail: Docs: "Claude can run them in parallel with asyncio.gather". Parallel calls arrive as several tool_use blocks in one paused response; "repeat Step 3 with a tool_result for every pending programmatic call in one user message". Elapsed time depends on the client. disable_parallel_tool_use: true is not supported with PTC.

P10.detail: Docs say exceptions surface in stderr: "Claude receives the error in stderr". The documented TimeoutError example has stderr text and "return_code": 0, so return_code alone does not flag the failure. Exact traceback format for a raised ValueError is not documented.

P11.detail: Docs name only "a small fixed overhead (container startup, script generation)". No latency figure.

P12.detail: Docs claim "Full isolation from host system and other containers". Not tested. Note: os.system and Bash are features inside the container (the tool runs Bash commands by design), so __import__('os').system('echo PWNED') would print inside the sandbox; the claim is about reaching Anthropic's host.

defaults.time: 90 s wall clock per REPL cell (PTC); about 4 min (270 s in the example) per pending host tool call; whole-call maximum unstated
defaults.output: stdout + stderr in code_execution_result; truncation threshold unstated
defaults.tool_calls: No count limit stated; each programmatic call counts toward normal tool-use rate limits

source_notes.finding: Client tools opt in with allowed_callers; the API turns them into async Python functions taking one dict and returning a string. SDK types accept direct, code_execution_20250825, code_execution_20260120, code_execution_20260521.
All opted-in tools are presented upfront; deferred loading via defer_loading + Tool Search Tool is a separate feature (tool_param.py defer_loading field).

Pause/resume over the Messages API. Code pauses at each call; the response has stop_reason tool_use and a tool_use block whose caller is {type: code_execution_20260120, tool_id: <server_tool_use id>}. The client replies with a user message of only tool_result blocks and must pass the container ID, or the API rejects it.

The SDK thread state copies the container ID from each reply into the next request automatically: "container-bound server tools reject a follow-up request that omits the container the previous turn ran in." A tool that raises becomes a tool_result with is_error: True.

mcp_tool() wraps an MCP ClientSession tool as a client-side runnable tool and accepts allowed_callers. Docs forbid programmatic calls to MCP connector tools, but MCP tools run client-side through this helper can be offered to code (inference from source; not run).
Container, not a language sandbox. Docs claim full host isolation, workspace-only file access, no internet.

Only the final code output enters context: "Tool results from programmatic calls are not added to Claude's context: Only the final code output is." Programmatic tool results also do not count toward token usage.
Tool errors are returned to the running code as tool_result text; code-level exceptions go to stderr.

Not ZDR or HIPAA eligible; container data retained up to 30 days. Tool results must be strings or text blocks (images rejected). strict: true tools, tool_choice forcing, and MCP connector tools are excluded. Not available in Managed Agents. Haiku 4.5 lacks PTC.

Docs report: agentic search benchmarks (BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA) +11% average with 24% fewer input tokens; a 75-tool benchmark -38% billed input tokens with no accuracy change; tau2-bench unchanged score at about 8% more cost.

surprises: The survey's opt-in value allowed_callers: ["code_execution_20250825"] is outdated. PTC now requires code_execution_20260120 or later, yet the SDK Literal still lists code_execution_20250825 as a caller value (tool_param.py:45-47).
allowed_callers is guidance, not enforcement: "it is not a hard API-level block on direct calls ... Do not rely on allowed_callers as a security boundary."
The documented TimeoutError result has return_code 0 with the error only in stderr.
Network inside the container is now documented as completely disabled (survey listed it as unverified).
Not ZDR eligible and data is retained up to 30 days, which matters for an investigations customer. OpenAI PTC supports ZDR.
On tau2-bench, PTC cost about 8% more with no score change; Anthropic says sequential single-call workflows do not benefit.
